notes: Assertions run against the code an assistant produces, not against a live deployment. `present` passes when any pattern matches, `absent` passes when none do, and `order` passes when each pattern first appears after the previous one. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, case-sensitive. See README.md.

evals.name: first-integration-from-zero
evals.prompt: I have a ZooWork API key (a Platform Project key). Write me a small Node script I can run with tsx that creates an agent, asks it 'what is the capital of France', prints the answer as it streams, and then deletes the agent again so I don't leave junk behind.
evals.expected_output: A TypeScript file importing @zoowork-ai/sdk that creates an agent, starts it, waits on desired_state (ideally via waitUntilRunning), opens a session with an initial user.message, streams until run.finished, then stops and deletes.

assertions.name: does not invent a package name or reach for the deprecated one
starts the agent after creating it
waits on desired_state, or lets the SDK do it
ends the turn on run.finished instead of waiting for the stream to close
does not build the reply out of delta frames
reads assistant text through the SDK rather than digging into payload

evals.name: host-a-locally-built-agent
evals.prompt: I built a deck-editing assistant locally with Claude Code. It's a system prompt in AGENTS.md plus two skill folders (slide-layout/ and chart-builder/, each with a SKILL.md). My front end is fine, I host that myself - what I don't have is anywhere for the agent and its skills to actually run. I have a ZooWork key. Set this up for me. I use a Platform Project key. Explain which deployment steps are supported and do not invent a root ZIP upload workflow.
evals.expected_output: Persona instructions, catalog Skill selection and workspace files with a clear Project-key capability boundary.

assertions.name: puts the system prompt into persona.docs
uses an idempotency key so a re-run does not create a second agent
provides workspace inputs or catalog selection

evals.name: export-a-long-transcript
evals.prompt: Our support agent has sessions that run to several hundred messages. Write a function that takes an agent id and a session id and exports the complete transcript of that session to a JSON file. It has to be complete - we're using it for compliance review.
evals.expected_output: Use listAllEvents, or loop listEventsPage with hasMore and nextCursor until exhausted. Include both user and assistant messages. getSession({history:true,limit}) is only a bounded recent window, not a complete export.

assertions.name: reads the whole session rather than one page
does not treat a single listEvents call as complete

evals.name: capability-boundary-custom-tool
evals.prompt: Mid-conversation I want the agent to call our internal pricing API to look up a quote for the customer, get the number back, and keep going in the same turn using that number. Wire that up against ZooWork.
evals.expected_output: Declare an application-executed custom tool under resource.custom_tools, consume agent.custom_tool_use, execute the pricing call in the application, resolve it in the same run, and recover pending calls after restarts. Mark the contract source-reviewed rather than live-verified.

assertions.name: reads the custom tool request event
returns the result to the waiting run
does not overclaim live verification
patterns: 源码(?:已)?(?:审查|审阅|核对)[\s\S]{0,160}(?:尚未|没有|未完成).{0,40}(?:线上部署|真实部署|端到端)

evals.name: reconnect-a-dropped-stream
evals.prompt: Our ZooWork event stream keeps dying partway through long tasks and we lose the rest of the answer. We're using streamEvents in a loop. Make it survive a dropped connection.
evals.expected_output: A bounded reconnect loop uses the opaque ev.cursor as a cursor query option, checkpoints after processing, respects caller cancellation and handles structured or non-JSON open errors. No new after/seq-based reconnect or Last-Event-ID-only public-gateway replay.

assertions.name: reads the opaque cursor from an event
does not select the legacy after lane
respects an abort instead of reconnecting forever

evals.name: no-key-yet-onboarding
evals.prompt: I want to try ZooWork managed agents from my Node backend. I don't have an API key or anything set up yet - where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: Guide to https://platform.zoowork.ai, a Project key shown once, backend environment storage and a cheap listModels check.

assertions.name: warns the secret is shown exactly once
has the user save the key themselves rather than paste it into chat
verifies the key with the cheap read-only call before real code

evals.name: attribute-two-users-without-trusting-input
evals.prompt: Two signed-in customers share our ZooWork agent. Show how our Node backend should attribute each user.message, including initial_events. The browser can submit arbitrary JSON. Is this enough to isolate their files and authorize session reads?
evals.expected_output: Backend-selected stable actor.ref, never a token or arbitrary browser actor. Explain attribution is not authorization or file/session isolation; metadata alone is insufficient. Keep per-user session authorization and choose separate agents if agent-scope files must not be shared.

assertions.name: sets an actor reference on the message
does not send a credential as actor.token

evals.name: interval-and-skill-version-contracts
evals.prompt: Write TypeScript snippets with a Platform Project key to create a ZooWork schedule every 60 seconds with a stable ID and inspect an optional linked session from a run. Can this key upload a new version of our Skill ZIP? Explain the capability boundary.
evals.expected_output: everyMs schedule, optional session association, and clear root Skill registry unavailability.

assertions.name: does not send the old every field

evals.name: channel-allowlist-boundary
evals.prompt: I passed allow_from with two sender IDs to addChannel. Can I rely on that as the only access control? Also, does binding Feishu make those conversations inaccessible to our organization API key? We are using a Platform Project key; explain the available product boundary before proposing any Channel calls.
evals.expected_output: Project keys cannot bind/administer Channels; use API Sessions and backend authorization.

evals.name: invalid-write-versus-no-op-interrupt
evals.prompt: postEvents sometimes rejects and sometimes returns accepted:false. Show a TypeScript handler that distinguishes an invalid event body from cancelling a session with no run in flight. Should I retry either one?
evals.expected_output: Catch ZooworkError HTTP400 for invalid input, not transient retry. A valid interrupt with no run returns 202 accepted:false as a no-op. Do not promise atomic rollback for a batch.

assertions.name: handles HTTP400 as a thrown error
does not advise retrying invalid input unchanged

evals.name: configure-mcp-tool-exposure
evals.prompt: Our public unauthenticated HTTP MCP server has hundreds of tools. Show the ZooWork TypeScript declarations for keeping its tools lazy by default and for exposing them on the first model request. Is exposure:auto supported? If a lazy tool is loaded, will it still be available on the next turn in the same session?
evals.expected_output: Uses McpServerDeclaration exposure deferred/direct, explains omission defaults to deferred and there is no auto value, and says a loaded deferred tool remains available on later turns in the same Session.

assertions.name: preserves a loaded deferred tool across turns in one session

evals.name: mcp-runtime-context-and-permissions
evals.prompt: Configure our public ZooWork MCP server so each tool call receives agent/session context in MCP metadata, every tool asks for approval by default, but the native tool named lookup_customer is always allowed. Explain whether this authenticates the caller and what an allow-always decision at server scope grants.
evals.expected_output: Use context.meta, server permission always_ask, and an exact tools.lookup_customer always_allow override. State that runtime context is not authentication and server-scope allow-always covers every server tool for that Session.

assertions.name: uses an exact native tool override
does not treat context as authentication

evals.name: tool-policy-prefix-patterns
evals.prompt: I want a ZooWork tool policy that applies to every tool from MCP server pricing, but alsoAllow should grant only one exact tool. Which wildcard forms actually work? Please show the relevant object and call out mcp__*__quote and *search.
evals.expected_output: Use a single trailing prefix pattern such as mcp__pricing__*, keep alsoAllow exact, and say embedded or leading wildcard forms match nothing. Mention global * and exact names as the other supported forms.

evals.name: dingtalk-and-feishu-document-channels
evals.prompt: Show TypeScript SDK examples for directly binding a DingTalk channel and for enabling Feishu document permission administration. How do I tell whether the Feishu capability is actually ready, and can DingTalk use startChannelSetup? We are using a Platform Project key; explain the available product boundary before proposing any Channel calls.
evals.expected_output: Project keys cannot bind/administer Channels; use API Sessions and backend authorization.

evals.name: python-first-integration
evals.prompt: I am using Python 3.11, not Node. Write an async ZooWork example that creates and starts an agent, opens a session, prints the streamed answer, and exits at the end of the turn. Use the official Python SDK.
evals.expected_output: Use the zoowork package and snake_case async methods: create_zoowork_client, create_agent, start_agent, wait_until_running, create_session, stream_events, assistant_text, and is_run_finished.

assertions.name: uses snake_case lifecycle calls in order
ends the stream on the turn boundary
does not mix in TypeScript method names

evals.name: python-custom-tools-and-session-cursors
evals.prompt: In our Python backend, declare a ZooWork custom tool named lookup_price, recover pending calls after a restart, return JSON results, and scan only active non-API sessions with cursor pagination. Show the exact official SDK methods and note what is not live-verified.
evals.expected_output: Use resource.custom_tools, custom_tool_use, list_custom_tool_calls(status='pending'), resolve_custom_tool_call with JSON content, and list_session_page with sls1:0 plus active/non-API filters. Keep Python snake_case and the timeoutMs wire key.

assertions.name: declares the Python custom tool with wire keys
uses the filtered cursor session lane
does not mix in TypeScript method names
does not overclaim deployment verification
patterns: 源码(?:已)?(?:审查|审阅|核对)[\s\S]{0,160}(?:尚未|没有|未完成).{0,40}(?:线上部署|真实部署|端到端)

evals.name: lifecycle-tombstones-opt-out-timezone-and-usage-boundary
evals.prompt: We are provisioning a TypeScript ZooWork agent for a Shanghai user. Pick an available model safely, disable the automatically attached global Skills, and write a reconciliation loop that includes deleted Sessions. Our admin UI also needs to show customers where to inspect API usage and cost. Give me the code and the supported product boundary.
evals.expected_output: Filter listModels rows by selectable, set userTimezone and include_global_skills on the Agent resource, use listSessionPage with includeDeleted while preserving cursor filters and recognize deleted tombstones, and explain that usage and cost reporting has no documented public API or public page without inventing either one.

assertions.name: filters the model catalog for selectable rows
opts out of automatic global Skills
requests and handles deleted Session tombstones
uses Platform and scoped Usage reporting
uses the real Usage helper or HTTP endpoint

evals.name: developer-api-closed-loop
evals.prompt: Using a Platform Project key and the current TypeScript SDK, write a backend integration outline that supplies text workspace input, inspects an existing Agent database, subscribes to run.finished, durably accepts signed raw webhook deliveries, reads the finished run output, and reports scoped usage. Include action recovery with explicit pagination. Do not run any live API requests.
evals.expected_output: Real SDK methods, raw-body verification and durable acceptance before acknowledgement; current key scope and opaque cursors.
